Pochettino's first two games in charge have been plagued by controversial moments, following a similar pattern during the club's dreadful start, which has left them 19th, inside the Premier League relegation zone and out of the Carabao Cup. messages.text: Great Britain end seven-year wait to reach Davis Cup semi-finals

metadata.summary: Great Britain have taken a step closer to ending their 11-year wait for a Davis Cup title, as Leon Smith's side advanced to the semi-finals with a thrilling 2-1 victory over Germany.
metadata.content: Davis Cup - Great Britain 2-1 Germany: Cameron Norrie guides side to first semi-finals appearance in seven years | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Davis Cup - Great Britain 2-1 Germany: Cameron Norrie guides side to first semi-finals appearance in seven years Great Britain advanced to Davis Cup semi-finals after beating Germany 2-1; Cameron Norrie defeated Jan-Lennard Struff before Alexander Zverev beat Arthur Fery to level match; Neal Skupski and Henry Patten won deciding doubles rubber to book tie against either Austria or Spain Thursday 26 November 2026 15:02, UK Image: Cameron Norrie beat Jan-Lennard Struff in Great Britain's Davis Cup quarter-final against Germany Great Britain have taken a step closer to ending their 11-year wait for a Davis Cup title, as Leon Smith's side advanced to the semi-finals with a thrilling 2-1 victory over Germany. Neal Skupski and Henry Patten outlasted Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz in a nail-biting second-set tiebreak to seal a 6-2, 7-6(8-6) win and end Great Britain's seven-year wait for a Davis Cup semi-final appearance. It came after world No 1 Alexander Zverev had drawn the tie level at 1-1 with a comfortable 6-3 6-2 win over Arthur Fery. metadata.summary: When Liam Delap joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he probably had ambitions of cementing himself as an elite Premier League No 9. Perhaps even positioning himself to be the heir to Harry Kane's throne for England.
metadata.content: Liam Delap has a chance to show Chelsea what they're missing when they travel to Nottingham Forest | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Liam Delap has a chance to show Chelsea what they're missing when they travel to Nottingham Forest Liam Delap has a chance to show former club Chelsea what they are missing as Xabi Alonso's side continue to struggle in attack without Joao Pedro; watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Premier League and Main Event on Friday Night Football; kick-off 8pm Callum Bishop Football Journalist Wednesday 25 November 2026 12:17, UK When Liam Delap joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he probably had ambitions of cementing himself as an elite Premier League No 9. Perhaps even positioning himself to be the heir to Harry Kane's throne for England. Less than a month later, Joao Pedro made the move to Stamford Bridge and suddenly, the landscape changed. He was not the first-choice striker at the club. What followed was an arduous campaign that brought three goals in 47 games and saw Delap succumb to what is now the fabled curse of the Chelsea No 9 shirt. A club-record move to Nottingham Forest in August has yet to truly revitalise his career either. But Oliver Glasner does have faith that there's a 20-goal-a-season striker hiding in the 23-year-old. metadata.summary: DP World Tour player MJ Daffue has vowed to ‘kick butt and be ready to go soon’, having been forced to miss the start of the season after being diagnosed with a brain tumour.
metadata.content: MJ Daffue: DP World Tour player vows to 'kick butt' in battle with brain tumour after HotelPlanner Tour promotion | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content MJ Daffue: DP World Tour player vows to 'kick butt' in battle with brain tumour after HotelPlanner Tour promotion MJ Daffue secured his DP World Tour card via the HotelPlanner Tour, having won twice this season and finished fifth in the season-long rankings; Daffue revealed on social media that doctors had found tumours after he was hospitalised with an infection Thursday 26 November 2026 14:38, UK Image: DP World Tour player MJ Daffue has revealed he is undergoing treatment for a brain tumour DP World Tour player MJ Daffue has vowed to ‘kick butt and be ready to go soon’, having been forced to miss the start of the season after being diagnosed with a brain tumour. Daffue won twice on the HotelPlanner Tour this season and finished fifth in the Road to Mallorca rankings, securing his DP World Tour card, before being hospitalised earlier this month for an infection that unearthed further health issues. The 37-year-old has since revealed two tumours were found, including one benign on the liver, with Daffue now undergoing treatment to address the one found in his brain. In a statement on his Instagram, Daffue said: "It's taken a while to post anything about this year because of the difficult time the past two weeks has been. metadata.summary: Michael van Gerwen is ready to take a pre-tournament scouting mission to Alexandra Palace ahead of his bid for a fourth World Darts Championship title next month, live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: Michael van Gerwen 'buzzing' for World Darts Championship and ready to take early trip to new-look Alexandra Palace | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Michael van Gerwen 'buzzing' for World Darts Championship and ready to take early trip to new-look Alexandra Palace Michael van Gerwen reached the Grand Slam of Darts semi-finals and is among the favourites for the World Darts Championship, beginning December 11 live on Sky Sports; Van Gerwen previously won the Sid Waddell Trophy in 2014, 2017 and 2019 Thursday 26 November 2026 14:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen says he is 'buzzing' ahead of the draw for the World Darts Championship on Monday Michael van Gerwen is ready to take a pre-tournament scouting mission to Alexandra Palace ahead of his bid for a fourth World Darts Championship title next month, live on Sky Sports . The Dutchman produced an impressive run to the Grand Slam of Darts semi-finals earlier this month, where he fired a nine-darter in the first leg of his quarter-final victory over Tom Sykes before being knocked out by compatriot Gian van Veen. Van Gerwen is keen to build on his Wolverhampton performance at this weekend's Players Championship Finals ahead of turning attention to the Worlds, where he will be among the favourites to lift the Sid Waddell Trophy.
